source.title: Product of the Last K Numbers

teaching.hint: What information about the most recent zero determines whether a suffix product can use division?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Product division works only inside a zero-free suffix; any query reaching across the latest zero must return zero.
solution_outline.approach: Keep cumulative products since the latest zero, starting with multiplicative identity 1. Reset that sequence on zero. For a query within the current suffix, divide the final cumulative product by the one before the requested suffix.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The stored sequence gives exact products of prefixes since the latest zero; its length records how many values followed that zero.
solution_outline.correctness: If `k` exceeds that length, the requested suffix contains zero. Otherwise the ratio of two nonzero prefix products cancels exactly the earlier factors.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(1)` amortized time per add and `O(1)` per query; `O(m)` space for the current zero-free suffix of length `m`.
solution_outline.pitfall: Keeping a cumulative product across zero makes division undefined and destroys later nonzero queries.

common_wrong_turns: Divide by a prefix product that may be zero
Scan the last k entries for every query
source_fidelity_notes: The varying `k`, zero value, valid query length, and constant-time follow-up are retained.
